assertions.rationale: I traced the code and the delivered tests for every corpus file, and each result matches the oracle. valid_parsed is accepted with 2 signals: Power/NEC and Vol_up/NECext with the right address and command bytes. valid_raw is accepted with 1 raw signal at 38000 Hz and 11 timings. Each of the other files is rejected: truncated ends mid-line and returns IR_ERR_TRUNCATED. too_many_timings is rejected at the 1025th timing. future_version gets IR_ERR_VERSION. wrong_filetype gets IR_ERR_HEADER. In overflow_values, frequency 4294967296 overflows the 64-bit-checked parse_u32 and returns IR_ERR_RANGE; separately, negative timings are rejected by the data scanner. duplicate_and_short_hex fails on the duplicate name (a stated rule: a new name is allowed only after a complete block), and parse_hex4 requires exactly 11 characters, so the 3-byte command would also be rejected. nonprintable_name is rejected on the ESC byte with IR_ERR_BAD_CHAR. long_line is rejected with IR_ERR_TOO_LONG at a fixed 63-character buffer. empty gets IR_ERR_EMPTY. instruction_in_name is accepted, with the name kept verbatim as data.

The supported keys are listed explicitly in the header and the final answer, and other keys are rejected. Address and command must be exactly 'XX XX XX XX' (len==11, four hex pairs), and inline tests check that 5-byte and non-hex values are rejected.

The v1 fields match the firmware format: Filetype 'IR signals file', Version 1, name/type/protocol/address/command/frequency/duty_cycle/data. The limits match the firmware too: 1024 timings, frequency 10k–56k, duty cycle in (0,1]. A custom streaming reader with no SDK dependency is reasonably justified by testability on a PC. Two deductions: FlipperFormat is never weighed as an alternative, and the header comment says the source 'builds in a FAP (API 88.2...)', which was never verified (the final answer does say it was not built as a FAP).

There is no heap allocation in the parser. Limits are explicit: 128 signals, 1024 timings, 63-character names, 15-character keys and protocols, at most 10 digits per token. Lines are streamed in constant memory. Integer parsing is overflow-safe (64-bit accumulator compared against UINT32_MAX), and duty cycle uses fixed point. Tests cover multi-megabyte input and include a mutation-fuzz loop run under ASan/UBSan.

The session actually ran `make test`, with ASan/UBSan flags in the Makefile, iterated on failures, and reported check counts and per-file results. It says plainly that nothing was built as a FAP or run on a device.

The answer makes no claim of full format support: it states the subset and says Version 2 and the library filetype are rejected. The extras (chunked feed and a describe helper for the UI) serve the stated FAP use case.
Limits, error codes with the line of the first error, the all-or-nothing rule, and policy choices (name length, ASCII only) are documented in the header and the final answer.
